paragraphs: 33 ALERTS sells printed QR code decals that let the people inside a venue report a problem by scanning a code with a phone camera. Reports range from facility complaints to suspicious activity, and the site is explicit that the service is not a replacement for 911.

A person opens the phone camera and scans the decal, with no download or account required. That sends a text message to the venue security operations center or response team carrying the exact location where help is needed. The receiving team can message the reporter back to ask questions. In arenas the placement is described down to section, row and seat.

Settings named on the site include colleges, universities and PK-12 schools, alongside stadiums, fairs, parks and airports. On campuses the decals are pitched as reaching places blue light emergency phones do not. The page carries a copyright notice for 33 Systems Inc., doing business as 33 ALERTS, of Tampa, Florida.

quote.text: Think of it as a private 911 system for venues.
